deviations.description: OpenML EMNIST_Balanced (41039) first 112800 rows, accepted only when class counts match the torchvision balanced train split; row identity and pixel orientation with torchvision are unverified (both irrelevant to an MLP)
label-permutation and example streams are seed-derived; upstream streams are unseeded
task blocks are [t*L, (t+1)*L); upstream logging is shifted one step
bias corrections remain float32; upstream mixes float64 scalars

notes: mechanism-transfer diagnostic: does EMA input conditioning (confirmed +0.061 vs published UPGD-W config at full horizon on Input-permuted MNIST, outputs/ipmnist_screening/confirm_full/) transfer to Label-permuted EMNIST?

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION (recorded before any v2 shard ran): L/P EMNIST inputs are STATIONARY (labels permute, pixel features never do), so input conditioning should transfer only weakly: predicted upgd_ema_norm minus v1 upgd_w (0.6715) small, |delta| <= ~0.02, far below the +0.061 IPMNIST effect; upgd_ema_norm_sigma0 expected ~= upgd_ema_norm (perturbation not load-bearing under conditioning); sgd_ema_norm (bare conditioning, no utility gate) predicted to collapse far below upgd_w, near the plain-optimizer band ~0.2-0.4, because the gate/consolidation machinery does the heavy lifting under label recurrence (UPGD-W rises 0.40->0.737 in v1 while AdamW sits at 0.20). A near-null conditioning effect here CONFIRMS the mechanism reading: conditioning fixes input non-stationarity, not label non-stationarity.
seeds 100,101,102 deliberately match plan.v1: schedule/init/noise streams are seed-derived, so per-seed paired deltas against the v1 upgd_w arm are meaningful
sgd_ema_norm weight_decay matched to the published EMNIST UPGD-W decay (0.0); the IPMNIST screening sgd_ema_norm used 0.01 to match that protocol's UPGD-W decay

normalized-arm factories are the pinned IPMNIST screening-lane implementations (ipmnist_screening._make_upgd_ema_norm_learner / _make_sgd_ema_norm_learner); norm_decay=0.999, norm_epsilon=1e-8 as screened and confirmed there

paper_reference.citation: Elsayed & Mahmood (2024). Addressing Loss of Plasticity and Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning. ICLR 2024.
paper_reference.qualitative: UPGD-W rises toward ~0.73-0.75 across 400 tasks; plasticity-only and plain-optimizer baselines sit near ~0.35.
